Dear Medical Director,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for Arthroscopic Meniscal Repair for my patient {{patient_name}}. The Clinical Compass™ Meniscal Repair Decision Support assessment yielded a recommendation of "[Meniscal Repair Recommendation]" (Class of Recommendation [COR]) based on the 2019 AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline for Meniscal and Articular Cartilage Lesions.

CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION:
• Patient presents with symptomatic meniscal tear with mechanical symptoms and functional impairment
• MRI-confirmed meniscal tear with favorable morphology for repair
• Patient age and activity level favor repair over meniscectomy
• Repair preserves meniscal function and prevents accelerated OA development

MEDICAL NECESSITY AND RATIONALE FOR REPAIR OVER MENISCECTOMY:
Arthroscopic Meniscal Repair is medically necessary and preferred over meniscectomy for this patient because:
1. Tear morphology (peripheral, vertical, adequate vascularity) is favorable for healing
2. Patient age [AGE] and activity level favor long-term meniscal preservation
3. Meniscectomy is associated with accelerated knee OA development (Salata et al., Sports Health 2010)
4. Repair preserves meniscal function — shock absorption, load distribution, joint stability
5. Meets AAOS criteria for repair over meniscectomy per 2019 Clinical Practice Guideline

GUIDELINE SUPPORT:
The 2019 AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline recommends meniscal repair over meniscectomy when tear morphology and patient factors are favorable for healing. Vertical longitudinal tears in the peripheral vascular zone have high healing rates (Pujol et al., AJSM 2008). Long-term outcomes are superior with repair compared to meniscectomy for preservation of knee function and prevention of OA (Nepple et al., AJSM 2012).

Without meniscal repair, this patient faces progressive meniscal deficiency, accelerated knee OA, and long-term functional decline. Meniscectomy, while technically simpler, sacrifices meniscal tissue and is associated with significantly higher rates of knee OA at 10-20 year follow-up.

I respectfully request immediate reconsideration and approval of prior authorization for Arthroscopic Meniscal Repair (CPT 29882). Please contact my office at {{practice_phone}} or {{practice_email}} if additional clinical documentation is required.
